answer.text: Budgeted excess of government expenditure over its revenue

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 96 of the NISM Series XV workbook, fiscal deficit is defined as the budgeted excess of Government expenditure over revenues in a specific year. It is generally expressed as a percentage of GDP. The Trap: Exports minus imports is the trade deficit (a current-account concept discussed on page 98), not the fiscal deficit. Revenue receipts minus revenue expenditure is the revenue deficit. Total debt is a stock concept, not the flow definition of fiscal deficit. Note: Source-backed definition from page 96 of Series XV: fiscal deficit = budgeted excess of Government expenditure over revenues in a specific year.
